subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management removal, should OpenClaw stale the routed session and remove the cached proactive conversation reference, stale only the session, or delete retained Teams transcript/session data?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable behavior controls personal-chat history and proactive reachability after app removal, so automation should not choose the privacy-retention boundary alone.

options.title: Stale session and clear cached reference
options.body: Use the existing non-destructive stale-session pattern while removing or tombstoning the stored Teams conversation reference so proactive sends cannot keep a removed app chat alive.

options.title: Stale only the routed session
options.body: Limit the fix to transcript-context isolation and accept cached proactive references as a separate follow-up risk.

options.title: Delete retained Teams data
options.body: Treat removal as a destructive retention boundary, which needs explicit data-loss policy, migration behavior, and stronger security review.

recommendation.title: Stale session and clear cached reference
recommendation.body: Use the existing non-destructive stale-session pattern while removing or tombstoning the stored Teams conversation reference so proactive sends cannot keep a removed app chat alive.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Teams conversation-store and security-sensitive state history makes this the best available owner for the retention-boundary choice.
